extraction.name: C-E VAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.description: A Chinese evaluation suite for foundation models consisting of 13,948 multiple-choice exam questions across 52 subjects and four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, professional), with a separate C-E VAL HARD subset for challenging reasoning tasks.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data were collected from real-world Chinese exams and exam-like sources. The authors selected subjects across middle school, high school, college, and professional levels, then collected questions from mock exams freely available on the internet, some past exam questions from top universities publicly shared by students, and a minor fraction of college-level mock graduate entrance exam questions from the Weipu website with authorization. The collected documents were parsed and annotated by the authors into a structured format.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams freely available on the internet; past exam questions from top universities publicly shared by students; a minor fraction of college-level mock graduate entrance exam questions from the Weipu website; source documents were primarily PDF and Microsoft Word documents, with a minor fraction as web pages.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were parsed into a structured format, complex mathematical notations were manually converted into standard LaTeX, questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, questions with more than four options had incorrect choices randomly dropped, and the data were deduplicated and cleaned.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were first processed into text; questions were then parsed automatically when possible and otherwise manually by the authors; all questions were standardized to exactly four choices; deduplication and cleaning were applied; human validation was performed in several rounds; LaTeX notations were checked to compile without syntax errors; the dataset was split into development, validation, and test sets within each subject.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually annotated parsed questions into a final structured format. For the development split, explanation data were created by prompting GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanations for ground-truth answers, then manually revising those explanations. The paper also states that some necessary manual annotation was performed from PDF or Word documents.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The collected data underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors. For explanation data, GPT-4-generated explanations were manually revised to obtain the final explanations. The paper also notes that the test labels are kept private for fair use.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate step-by-step explanations for the development split before manual revision.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Development and validation labels are released, while test labels are kept private. Users submit predictions to the website to obtain test accuracy, and a public leaderboard is maintained. Users may optionally include their submission results in the live leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve evaluation of foundation models for Chinese users and to help analyze strengths and shortcomings of models in a Chinese context. The paper also notes broader concerns about safety, bias, and robustness as future evaluation directions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases toward the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them. C-E VAL is designed to better reflect Chinese users' primary interests and Chinese society. The paper also reports option distribution fluctuations, though relatively small around random chance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to multiple-choice questions and accuracy-based evaluation. Some subjects are not reasoning-intensive, so chain-of-thought prompting may not help and can hurt performance. The test labels are private, and the benchmark may still be subject to data contamination from web-crawled pretraining data. The paper also notes that C-E VAL is far from perfect for LLM evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of foundation models and LLMs in zero-shot, five-shot, answer-only, and chain-of-thought settings; development split is used for few-shot exemplars and explanation data; validation split is intended for hyperparameter tuning; test split is used for benchmark evaluation via submitted predictions.
